prompt: In classical two-valued logic, what is $\neg\neg P$ equivalent to? Here $Q$ is a separate, independent statement.

answers.explanation: Negation flips a truth value. Flipping it twice restores the original value, so $\neg\neg P$ and P agree in both cases.
One negation flips the value; two restore it.
The truth of an unrelated statement Q does not determine P.
Negating an unrelated statement cannot express double negation of P.

This can be true when P is false, unlike double negation of P.
This is always true, while double negation has P’s value and can be false.
